You need to add Line Order as well. But it works on principle of string sort. In this case 11 is not eleven but one one. And 11  is lower than 2. First you sort first digit from 0 to 9, then you do the same sort on the 2nd digit etc.

If you have to sort numbers from 1 to 10, it would be :  1,10,2,3, etc. If you have to sort numbers from 1 to 200, your order would be 1,10,100,101,102....

Hey hey! To summarise what's happening here and highlight the concerns with possible solution.
To clarify on the buttons.
IOT Reboot - It's used when we know that there might be issues with tracking/losing GPS internet connection to send out commands to the car. Can be also used when the doors are not unlocking/locking. It does not however unlock the vehicle, this is where the button
Unlock Car Door comes in.
That button does have legitimate use-cases. I.e when after rebooting, user is still struggling with unlocking the door and is right next to the car. _However_, there are bad actor cases as mentioned above, where users do get clear error message of being far off from the car and ask CS to unlock the doors. What that essentially does is:
User has an active booking with unlocked car that they can start and ride with, then later cancel the booking.
*This is what we want to avoid.*
What we'd like is for CS to verify that user is actually close to the car and explicitly ask from user, what kind of an error message they see when trying to unlock a car. If it's too far error message - then they instruct the user to get to the car and try again.
One other part about this though is there might be edge cases, where user actually is close to car, yet either phone's GPS is off or the Cars. *In this case, agents need to try rebooting IoT and also ask user to close/open the app (also checking GPS settings can't hurt).*

Hope that clears up some misunderstandings 😄

Some context from Ragnar (Eater):

We had some reports come in that were linked to {{isInternetReachable}}

* By default it uses a Google endpoint for checks, but in rare cases some users might have it blocked (now we found out that the culprit was Adguard [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/TECH-56597|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/TECH-56597|smart-link] ) This could be potentially avoided if the endpoint is on our domain.
* There's a RN bug with fetch request failing on iOS if it happens while app is in background state ([https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/35384|https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/35384|smart-link] , [https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/29908|https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/29908|smart-link] ). We did patch this issue in eater though [https://github.com/bolteu/food-delivery-eater-app/blob/dev/patches/%40react-native-community%2Bnetinfo%2B9.3.6.patch|https://github.com/bolteu/food-delivery-eater-app/blob/dev/patches/%40react-native-community%2Bnetinfo%2B9.3.6.patch] 
* If showing some error UI, having at least two consecutive failing requests for it is best, otherwise it will be too sensitive

{{isConnected}} should always be reliable as it uses the native API and shouldn't give false positives, but it won't cover case where wifi is connected, but it can't actually reach the internet (this can be simulated if on iPhone go to Developer -> Network linker -> 100% loss)

In Eater the user would eventually see an error message in such case from a failing API call and it should be enough of a hint that something isn't right, RH has used the same approach

Happy to cover your concerns:

{{the historic data related to any trips taken on our platform will (and should!) stay intact. Aside from insurance claims, what if someone commits a crime using our scooters, and the police need the data for investigation? Deleting one's user account from our platform should not become a tool to protect oneself from legal consequences.}}

Under the GDPR we should delete all data that we have about a user once we no longer need this data for our intended purposes. For insurance claims, we are now trying to understand the period within which we can claim that we still have a purpose to retain this data. 

In terms of police requests, if we still have data in our systems even once the account is deleted, we have a legal obligation (legal basis - Art 6(1)(c) of the GDPR) to share this data with the police. But if we have already deleted this data and cannot find them on our system, we can reject the police request since no data found in our systems. That’s how privacy law works and that’s why we need to align on the term we need this data for covering insurance claims (that can include police requests within this period of time as well).

{{So to sum up, I see no issues with us sharing the trip information with our insurance provider, especially considering that Bolt has a contractual obligation to hand over that data to the insurance provider (GDPR 6c). See the highlighted part of the contract below, please.}}

Unfortunately, we cannot rely on Art 6(1)(c) for sharing this data with insurance companies since Art 6(1)(c) refers only to the legal obligation provided for in the legal acts, not in the commercial agreements. But we have another legal basis to share this data with them - legitimate interest. No worries on this part - we’re on it.🙂

*Privacy Implications I see:*
1. General risk from the CCTV in place: Potential lack of employee’s notification about the CCTV in place and failure to ensure the employee’s right to object to the surveillance in accordance with Article 21
2. 30-day period for retaining these images can be too extensive especially in some markets. It would be great to reduce this period especially in the situation where we are not sure if we are going to involve the police.
3. If we are going to share these CCTV images with the outside attorney, we should ensure that we have a legal basis to do so, but for sharing with the police we do have a legal basis.

import os
import mysql.connector

# MySQL connection configuration
config = {
    'user': 'root',

    'database': 'tidb_cdc',
}

# Connect to the MySQL server
try:
    connection = mysql.connector.connect(**config)
except mysql.connector.Error as err:
    print("Error connecting to MySQL:", err)
    exit(1)

# Fetch the row with the highest primary_ts for each cf
query = "SELECT cf, MAX(primary_ts), MAX(secondary_ts) FROM tidb_cdc.syncpoint_v1 GROUP BY cf ORDER BY cf;"

try:
    cursor = connection.cursor()
    cursor.execute(query)
    rows = cursor.fetchall()

    if rows:
        for row in rows:
            cf, primary_ts, secondary_ts = row

            # Strip 'default_' from the start and replace '-' with '_'

######################### Global config #########################

[task]
    output-dir = "./output-{cf}"
    source-instances = ["mysql1"]
    target-instance = "tidb0"
    target-check-tables = ["{cf}.*"]
'''

            # Write the configuration to a file named after the cf value
            filename = f"{cf}.toml"
            with open(filename, 'w') as f:
                f.write(config_heredoc)

#            print(f"Configuration written to {filename}")

            # Execute the command using subprocess
            cmd = f"/home/leandro/tidb-community-toolkit-v6.5.1-linux-amd64/sync_diff_inspector --config=./{filename}"

* yes, sharing accounts with third parties is not allowed. Proper identification should be in place, for the business team to ensure it.

* for selling alcohol a courier must be a least 18 y.o. Minor couriers (16-17) could be engaged (but not for alcohol delivery) in certain cases if they have a proper registration for tax purposes. If the account is shared, clearly there is a risk that third parties are below 18 or even 16 and do not have a proper tax registration.

If we got information about the place where allegedly people can lease couriers' accounts and bags:

* we should check the correctness of the information (do some investigation);
* identify couriers whose accounts are shared. If couriers knowingly allowed sharing of their accounts, is it a ground for suspension from the platform (clause 9.1 of T&C for partners);
* if such illegal activities, indeed, take place, we should engage the police to ensure such activities are stopped.

Hey!

Noted!

# We understand the question about the safety of the road users and we have no objections to the fact that head injuries can have unforeseen consequences for the injured party. Thus the topic should viewed as a whole and have uniform rules, without differentiating between regular-, business- and bicycle users.
# E-scooters have, by the applicable regulations, speed limitations. This means, an e-scooter cannot travel faster than 25 km/h - this is onto its own a significant safety measure. Bicycles don’t have speed limiters and the electronic limiter can be overridden by manually cranking the gears. Usually the local municipalities set their own applicable speed limit, limiting the possible harmful effects further.
# Comparing an e-scooter and a regular bike - both users are exposed to the environment and have nothing to protect them from side impacts or front moving acceleration. If the safety is the concern, then the helmet requirement should be applicable to all less protected road users, not only the e-scooter ones. 
# Current applicable legislation doesn’t impose the safety helmet for bicycle users (only for children). If the helmet is made mandatory for electric scooter use, but not for bicycles, this leaves the question - what are the proven grounds for such distinction? As per definition of the bicycle in LV law, they can have an auxiliary electric motor, that can accelerate up to 25 km/h. Will this mean that all the electric bicycles are also included in the scope? If the differentiating factor is human muscle power, then an e-scooter needs human muscle power for operating, which leaves us yet again with uncertainty as such limitation does not have legal clarity to be justified - any limitation should serve a purpose and defend some grater good.
# If the limitation is applied to one group of vehicles, but not the other, we will have a situation, where one type of vehicle (and associated businesses) are more favoured than the others. Mandatory helmets for electric scooters will generate additional costs for the operators, while bicycle rental business can do without them. This seems to be unfair advantage that is given to a similar business, without serving a greater good or specific goal. While we acknowledge that sometimes positive measures are needed for developing certain areas of public services and relevant businesses, currently the proposed measure gives unjustified and confusing advantage that has no merit. 
# In addition, it’s not clear how the limitation would be applied - if the goal is to increase the road safety, the same rules should apply for private users and operators. It should be applicable to scooters, bicycles, e-bikes, electric scooters, monocycles, hoover boards etc. The best way to increase the safety of vulnerable road users is to limit the speed of cars - it’s easier to decrease the kinetic energy of a 2 ton vehicle than to protect 70 kg of human from the impact.

* In the right setup, the taxi fleet should have informed Bolt about the driver's death (because taxi drivers are engaged with Bolt indirectly via the employment by taxi fleets) and requested account deletion (or delete the account itself if the fleet has such permission).
* Since the taxi fleet clearly acted in violation of T&C or even in bad faith, we have to get in touch with it, explain the order, in particular, that driver’s individual accounts cannot be shared with third parties, and if a driver passes away or just leaves, the fleet shall close the account and in no circumstances allow its use by another person.
* If Bolt learns about the driver passing away, it makes sense to inform the taxi company that employed the driver that the account will be deleted due to said reason. If the driver was an independent driver, a fleet shall not be informed. I assume it is ok to delete the account if we have no doubts that the information about a driver’s passing away is correct. We used to have some issues with dates overlapping. This happens in case something is added or updated in the balance for that period (22nd to 31st of [MONTH]) after the [MONTH] invoice was created (2nd of [MONTH]). In this case, those items which were added later will be included in the next month's invoice and the period is extended accordingly. We indeed did not intend to invoice twice that period and the row only includes the 1st to the 31st of [MONTH]. This issue has been resolved by devs recently. Please advise to drivers or fleet owners to re-download the invoices, this should be fixed for now.

While testing the changes, I noticed that reading the registration table can be a bit slow. It was a view model, but also some partition key filters were missing from metrics etc. 

Then I switched it to incremental. So the model will be materialised incrementally and not updated if the source has updates. This means:

* we don’t get the most up to date information on ‘is_duplicated’, we get the state as it was when loaded
* we can compare this against the source to see how much it changes



So I guess it would be good to do the switch.

We still need the privacy policy for couriers since after personal data is transferred to Bolt by fleets, we process this data for our purposes and need to inform couriers about this processing.

*How we should work with fleets:*
1. Recently, *we have created the* [*Data Sharing Agreement* |https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GCYC-FoHIy17YRrWPeNrAJen8ej-rw4h/edit]*for all markets* governing cases when the Fleet shares Couriers' data with Bolt via Registration Form on Bolt's website or by other means, and the data is then processed by Bolt for couriers' registration onto Bolt Food Platform. As fas as I know*,* [~accountid:63da287e790148a18093a774] has updated the main template agreement with fleets for all markets and added this DSA to this main template.
2. If fleets register their couriers via the registration form on our website (similar to [the one we have in LT|https://courier.bolt.eu/lithuania-fleet-form-2sha43546r7tuyghjchfxdrste578yugkjfyu]), we s*hould place the following wording on the site:*

“You hereby confirm and represent to Bolt that by providing any Personal Data to Bolt, You possess a valid legal basis for the disclosure and Processing of such Personal Data. Furthermore, You assure that the respective Data Subjects (i.e., Couriers) have been duly informed about the Processing activities pertaining to their Personal Data before providing their Data to Bolt.

In compliance with Data Protection Legislations, You shall provide the Data Subjects (i.e., Couriers) with a clear and conspicuous link to the Privacy Policy of Bolt (link to the Privacy Policy available at [http://www.food.bolt.eu/legal|http://www.food.bolt.eu/legal|smart-link] ), which acts as an independent controller responsible for Processing the Personal Data received from You.”.

3. *The Privacy Policy should be specified in this wording* and conveyed by the fleet to the couriers before sharing details with Bolt.
4. At the same time, *Bolt still has an obligation to inform about data processing* via the courier app (before the courier is logging in to the app after the registration by Bolt and during the whole journey of the app usage).

5. *We will create the Privacy Policy for Portugal since it’s inevitable part of our obligation to inform.* Could you please help understand if the processing activity in Portugal has different setup from other countries? Hi again [~accountid:641d70192cee496759ec78f0] 

Please find the answer below from the police:

Legal support for data requests. There are at least three different supports for when personal data may be provided to the Police Authority's law enforcement activities; if there is an obligation to provide information according to law, if it is not incompatible with the collection purpose and if, after a balance of interests, it appears to be necessary for purposes relating to the legitimate interests of the personal data controller or a third party and if the interests and fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject do not outweigh. The police authority has a very strong legitimate interest in processing personal data to fight crime. Even if there is no constitutional obligation to provide information or if it would be incompatible with the collection purpose to disclose information to the police, disclosure should therefore as a rule be permitted after a balance of interests in the individual case. This applies regardless of the legal basis used to collect the data. With reference to the confidentiality legislation, the Police Authority is prevented from giving a detailed account of the background to the request or explaining why the need arose. The police authority's view is thus that in a balance of interests made according to article 6.1 f, the authority's mission to fight crime must always be taken into account and that this is an important public interest. The authority is responsible for only requesting data if there is a concrete need and legal prerequisites for processing the personal data. A private actor can thus, when balancing his interests, always assume that the Police Authority has such a strong legitimate interest in taking part in the requested information, even if it cannot be explained in detail due to confidentiality. Worth noting in this context is that confidentiality normally applies to information within the framework of a criminal investigation, i.a. with the support of ch. 18 Sections 1 and 2 and Chapter 35 Section 1 of the Publicity and Confidentiality Act. The rules in the EU's data protection regulation (GDPR) thus do not prevent private actors from disclosing personal data to the Police Authority's law enforcement activities. The police authority has the right to process personal data for law-enforcement purposes with support in ch. 2. Section 1 of the Act (2018:1693) on the police's processing of personal data within the scope of the Criminal Data Act. 
Sincerely Tim Maxner

Hi Victor,

Thank you for reaching out! The number of stock option units depends on the position and is viewed as part of the *total compensation package* together with the annual base salary. The number of options is calculated as a % of annual base salary taking into account the recommended equity range for the role.

Stock option units are primarily granted when an employee joins the company _(new hire grant)_, in the case of a _promotion_ (granted to someone who is being promoted or whose job is changing and therefore their total compensation is reviewed) or when the employee has fully vested their initial grant, due to which equity compensation is reviewed _(grant refresh)_. Stock units are not increased by default, and any increase is primarily tied to the occasions mentioned above. 

All the best,
Katarina Ilves-Võtti

{quote}Velosipēdu ķiveres ir viens no tiem tematiem, kas bieži izraisa asas diskusijas. Taču sabiedrībā publiskas debates par ķiverēm nav nekas jauns. Jau vairākkārt ir notikušas kampaņas, lai palielinātu ķiveru lietošanu pilsētas velosipēdistu vidū.

Piemēram, 2008. gadā Kopenhāgenā plaša mēroga kampaņas, kuras mērķis bija veicināt ķiveru lietošanu, rezultātā velosipēdu pārdošana samazinājās par pieciem procentiem un nākamajā gadā pēc kampaņas pilsētā iebrauca par 10 000 mazāk velosipēdistu.

Tomēr ir daudz pierādījumu tam, ka braukšana ar velosipēdu kļūst drošāka, jo vairāk ir velosipēdistu. Labi piemēri ir Dānija un Nīderlande, kur ir daudz velosipēdistu, bet ļoti maz ķiveru. Nīderlandē 27 % no visiem braucieniem tiek veikti ar velosipēdu, bet ķiveres valkā mazāk nekā 1 % velosipēdistu.

Tāpēc mērķis ir nevis samazināt velosipēdistu skaitu, bet gan to palielināt. Lai to panāktu, mums ir vajadzīga pilsētvide, kas ļauj droši braukt ar velosipēdu. To nerada velosipēdists ar ķiveri, bet gan, pirmkārt, samazinot ātruma ierobežojumus pilsētās.

Ķivere ir paredzēta, lai aizsargātu galvu tieša trieciena gadījumā. Vairumā gadījumu cilvēks netrāpa tieši pret zemi galvas priekšā. Ķiveres mērķis ir aizsargāt personu dzīvībai nedraudoša viena transportlīdzekļa negadījuma gadījumā, ja ātrums ir mazāks par 20 km/h (20 mph). Neviena ķivere nepasargā braucēju no sadursmes ar automašīnu.

Eiropas Riteņbraucēju federācijas (EFC) oficiālā zinātniski pamatotā nostāja ir tāda, ka ķivere padara braukšanu ar velosipēdu pilsētā bīstamu, lai gan varbūtība, ka cilvēks gūs bojā, braucot ar velosipēdu, ir mazāka nekā ejot kājām.

Tāpat, kad sociālajos tīklos pajautāju Mikaelam Kolvillam-Andersenam, pazīstamam Dānijas mobilitātes ekspertam, vai, braucot pilsētā ar velosipēdu, ķivere ir nepieciešama, viņš atbildēja viennozīmīgi: "Ķivere ir bezjēdzīga un samazina cilvēku skaitu, kas brauc ar velosipēdu". Ļoti pamācošs ir viņa pirms 12 gadiem rīkotais TEDx pasākums "Kāpēc mums nevajadzētu braukt ar velosipēdu ar ķiveri", kurā viņš norāda, ka statistiski gājējiem un automobiļu pasažieriem ir lielāks risks gūt galvas traumas nekā velosipēdistiem, un ironiski ierosina, ka arī viņi varētu valkāt ķiveres.

Bezgalīgajā publiskajā stāstījumā, kas koncentrējas uz riteņbraucēju, gājēju un motorolleru vadītāju pamācīšanu, bieži vien netiek ņemta vērā autovadītāja loma un atbildība. *Southampton:*

* Send a reminder to the driver, informing them of their driver conditions to display vehicle signage. Ask the driver to provide photo evidence of their correct signage within 3 days.

If the driver has not provided evidence of correctly displayed signage within 3 days:

* Check the PHV (Private Hire Vehicle) start date for the driver.
* If the start date is on or after 1st July 2023, the new signage policy should be mandatory for such drivers, and they should not be offered Bolt signage. Instead, follow the same process as for drivers in *Other cities.*
** If the start date is before 1st July 2023 and the driver has not provided evidence of correctly displayed signage within 3 days, take the following actions:
** If the driver is still under the old policy (using Bolt signage), escalate the ticket to Tier 2.
** In Tier 2, block the driver from selecting the incorrect or missing signage (UK) block.
** Choose the duration as Infinite for the block.
** Escalate the ticket to Ops for further review and action.
** Inform the driver that they need to switch to the new policy if they haven't done so already. Starting from 1st July 2023, the new signage policy is mandatory for all new licences issued (including renewals).

Hey [~accountid:5e8716509126d30c240a7d65], [~accountid:5dcebc6199e7ea0c60b0f56c], thank you for your comments.

The obligation to send the money to the driver is on us due to the fact that we are merely an agent in receiving the money from the rider and sending them to the driver, since the money belong to the driver and not to us. Re fraud - correct, in case of fraud the driver should not have received the money anyway, so we should not send the payouts to them.

In case there is no fraud but another violation by the driver, the case is a bit different. Still, there is no strict requirement in Ukraine for that and I do not belive that the risk for not sending such payouts would be great. Therefore, in cases on other violations which are not fraud, we can refer to clause 4.9 of the T&Cs:

_4.9. Bolt may adjust the Fare for a particular order completed, if we detect a violation (such as taking a longer route, not stopping the fare meter of the Bolt App after the Transportation Services have been completed, starting the ride/waiting time before the Driver arrives to the pickup location or other abuse of Bolt Platform leading to artificial price increase) or in case a technical error affecting the final fare is identified._ +*_Bolt may also reduce or cancel the fare_*+ *_in case we have reasonable cause to suspect fraud_* +*_or a complaint by the Passenger indicates a violation by you._*+ _Bolt will only exercise its right to reduce or cancel the fare in a reasonable and justified manner._

Specifically for the driver mentioned in this ticket, we can use such clause 4.9. Also, his attorney is referencing that we breached the employment laws but not making the payout, but the driver +is not our employee.+ The driver also accepted this because clause 10.2 of our General Terms states the following - _You acknowledge that no employment agreement nor an employment relationship has been or will be established between you and us. You also acknowledge that no joint venture or partnership exists between you and us. You may not act as an employee, agent or representative of us nor bind any contract on behalf of us. If due to the implication of mandatory laws or otherwise, you shall be deemed an employee of us, you hereby agree to waive any claims against us that may arise as a result of such implied employment relationship._ Therefore, all references by the attorney to the employment laws are incorrect. This driver also breached some other clauses of our T&Cs as well as possibly the laws of Ukraine which prohibit supporting the war - I believe we are free to not send the money to him.

Hi [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] here is my proposal do address this question - thanks for your feedback!

I understand that Ops is implementing changes regarding blocking of drivers in the context of safety incidents. The proposal is to deploy a) an investigative block and b) permanent or hard block. Drivers will be blocked and their fleet operators will be informed weekly of all safety incidents regarding the drivers at their service. 

As a note, I believe it is very positive the attempt of involving fleet operators by the implementation of reporting of all safety events to them. 

Regarding the particular questions, they appear to be of safety nature and therefore I recommend that you *open a ticket with the safety to ensure alignment with them*. Additionally, please *submit a ticket for the privacy team to confirm with them whether the driver profiling requires any further compliance step*s.

However, from a reclassification point of view please see my thoughts below.

_QUESTION 1 “Regulate hard-blocks on high-risk or significant events. To mitigate the risk of driver reclassification and ensure fairness, we aim to establish a process for standardizing cases that warrant a permanent hard blocking. We believe it is crucial to involve the input of our legal team to ensure complete alignment and compliance. By doing so, we can make informed decisions and apply permanent hard blocks consistently and fairly.”_ 

* Our TVDE operator t&c establish that “18.4. Pursuant to article 14 (2) of Law no. 45/2018, of 10 August, Bolt is under the legal obligation to block the access to the Bolt Services to the TVDE Operators, Drivers at their services or vehicles that are not compliant with the legal requirements provided in the mentioned law, in the event of such violations being known to Bolt.”. Blocking outside this framework would appear to increase the reclassification risk, as is the case of the blocking now under review.
** Information to the fleet operator is positive. Nevertheless, why do we block drivers and not fleets, when we only have an agreement with fleets? Is it because we are under a position of power and exercise labour powers over the driver, including disciplinary power, such as the exclusion from future activities on the platform by deactivating the account? It can be argued that yes, which means that Bolt fulfils 2 reclassification criteria in Portugal and is at risk. Hence the suggestion is to (*a) ensure the communication re blocking is sent to the fleet and the driver as well (b) ideally put in place a process to allow fleet to block drivers (c) put in place process determining when are fleets blocked and not only drivers*: what is the consequence of the weekly communication to fleets? if a fleets receives safety events on more than 50% of their drivers, does anything happen or does it make sense to happen to the fleet?

_QUESTION 2 “Regulating hard-blocks on minor events, in cases where these events are frequently reported, and can pose a safety risk.”_

* I have concerns with the following 2 categories of safety events: driver displays unprofessional behaviour (ex car smocking) and driver is unfit for driving (ex fatigated). How do these categories fit under safety? Is this an indirect way of determining behaviour of drivers namely regarding their conduct towards the client? Hence, I recommend the r*eview of the categories with the safety team to ensure that they only include safety related events and a legal obligation is potentially at breach (the highway code, penal code…)*.

Finally, I suggest to ensure the appeal systems is part of the decision flow in the document. 

Please let me know if you need further information or clarification. If not, please confirm I can close the ticket.

Please see my analysis that can be sent to the restaurant:

”Bolt and the Partner are acting as separate data controllers in this relationship. Once the Client places an order, Bolt shares certain personal data with the Partner under the Data Sharing Agreement concluded between Bolt and the Partner for processing an order. When the data is shared, the Partner becomes a data controller for this data and can process it for its purposes and means. Hey [~accountid:60b0a48fd435380069b90208] , please see a few considerations below:

# It is ok to set a recommended (not strictly required) bag size because this is an objective requirement related to the provision of services and not to the courier himself, thus should not increase the reclassification risk. Highlight the opportunity to take Bolt’s bag if the courier does not have his own.
# We should be very careful with blocking couriers, it could be done in exception cases as this is a very severe punishment. Clause 4.7 states _“If the Courier has materially breached its obligations or has received_ +_several complaints_+_, Bolt has the right to temporarily or permanently suspend the Courier from using the Bolt Food Platform“._ Thus, I suggest if we receive a complaint about the damaged food, you send a courier a kind request to be more careful and possibly adjust the mode of transport, because larger orders delivered by bike could likely get damaged. If despite the warning we receive another complaint about the same courier regarding damaged food, then you can suspend him for a while relying on clause 4.7.
# We cannot request couriers to use a specific means of transport. Clause 3.1. of the T&C _“The Couriers may choose the means for providing the delivery service at their own discretion”._ As self-employed a courier could decide how and by using which means to provide services. If we start imposing transportation requirements, this will increase the reclassification risk.

Likewise- it was a pleasure and best of luck in the future!

We will make sure that this project is covered within the handover.

about “{color:#0747a6}*aren’t*{color} {color:#0747a6}*sharing personal data that can be re-identified”,* {color}maybe I get it wrong? why should it be impossible to re identify the data (eg. 1 data sat: privacy counsel, Bolt, South Africa → This would be possible with publicly available info).

Are the data transmitted in aggregated form (i.e. without reference between individual data points such as seniority, location, salary) or is a set in which various data such as salary, seniority, age, function, location are assigned to an unnamed person transmitted via the "Workday" system. If there is a reference between several data points regarding a person, the data at least allow that a person is identifiable. → Personal data


{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
A person is identifiable if the information is not sufficient in itself to assign it to a person, but it is possible as soon as the information is combined with other information. If it is possible to identify the person with the help of other available information and other means. Thus, all objective factors, such as the cost of identification and the time required, shall be taken into account. *In particular, the technologies available at the time of processing as well as technological developments shall be taken into account.*

*Knowledge and the means of third parties:* The GDPR does not provide any clear indications as to whether a relative or absolute reference to a person is to be assumed _(if the establishment of the reference to a person depends on the respective controller, this is referred to as a relative reference to a person; if the view is taken that it is sufficient that any third party can establish the reference to a person, this is referred to as an absolute reference to a person)._ In order to determine whether an individual is identifiable, account must be taken of all the means likely, in all probability, to be used *by the controller or by any other person* to identify the natural person. According to recital 26, the means to be explicitly considered in assessing the question of identifiability are those *that may be used by "another person" "to identify the individual directly or indirectly."* An absolute consideration could be inferred here. However, the use of the means by the third party must be *"reasonably likely."* This speaks in favor of a relative understanding, since the third party must come into contact with the data in question, e.g., it must have been transmitted to him. At the very least, however, according to recital 26, the conclusion seems permissible that it is not sufficient that any person anywhere in the world could establish the personal connection.
The ECJ's case law on the personal reference of IP addresses (Breyer) also indicates a relative understanding.
{panel}

Hi [~accountid:5df3830c73b0bd0e4d835499] - I’m still not satisfied from a GDPR perspective that we can release this data.

For us to release data to any 3rd party, we require a legal basis for the request. The legal basis provided by the police to this stage only applies to banks and credit payment companies; Bolt is neither of these. 

We need to establish we have the correct basis in law before we can provide the data. My suggestion is that we discuss our concerns with the police and ask them to provide an appropriate legal basis before we provide this data.

Also, as a general principle, we do not provide Rider ID, Driver ID, or Order ID to any 3rd party in any event. We would also not provide the vehicle registration since this is the personal data of the Driver.

Further, we need to ensure that any data released to any 3rd party is relevant to their  request. Since this is a violent crime investigation, we would not provide the price, search category, or group of search categories.

Meeting with Fin Planning, some notes:

* most of the reporting is currently done in spreadsheets combined to admin panel automation (much of the automation is integration with spreadsheets)
* Financial planning is about redistributing the budgets between all cities (participating in Fin planning) within restrictions set by campaigns analysts
* campaign analysts set restrictions based on:
** models predicting the GMV and the response curve for discounts
** heuristics about events on the market
** heuristics about seasonality. *NOTE*: there’s rarely robust evidence about the seasonally different impact of ads. So there’s most often an heuristic based on general market seasonality or level of mobility on the market
* There’s evidence from experiments about the impact of discounts, but it is not always aligned and non-controversial (even though experiments are organised every week). So the interval for decision making is also quite high. So business heuristics also take place
The Bolt Plus offer is required for this test.

Hi,

I understand that Ops is implementing changes regarding blocking of drivers in the context of safety incidents and that the proposal is to better define the process around investigative blocks and permanent or hard blocks. The idea seems to be that drivers will be blocked and their fleet operators will be informed weekly of all safety incidents regarding the drivers at their service.

As discussed in our meeting, I believe it is very positive the attempt of involving fleet operators by the implementation of reporting of all safety events to them.

However, as discussed before, blocking drivers might be seen as fulfilling criteria 2, 3, 4 and/or 5 of the ATD Law. While it seems very difficult not to control or supervise the activity of the drivers, you might remember that DLA was pretty clear in their advice: the only way to avoid meeting those criteria is to go through the fleet and say to the fleet that a client complained about a driver so can the fleet please do something to address this issue. If the fleet doesn't do anything, DLA advised that Bolt should envisage imposing a penalty first (to the fleet), and then could potentially block the fleet (not the driver) after a few events if the fleet hasn’t done anything. +Disabling the driver if the fleet doesn't do it would be very risky+.

Based on this, any blocking done by Bolt directly on the driver is a risk. So while Legal can advise on the wording to be used for the communication sent to the driver and the fleet for blocking, there is not particular was to mitigate the risks.

*_1. Regarding the document shared with us_*, I recommend that you *open a ticket for the Risk and Safety Team to ensure alignment with them*.

_Nb: Some categories of safety events (driver displays unprofessional behaviour (ex car smocking) and driver is unfit for driving (ex fatigated)) seem difficult to assess and do not correspond to legal obligations - it would seem better to ensure that categories only include safety related events where a legal obligation is potentially at breach (the highway code, penal code…)._

*_2. From a reclassification point of view_*, Emilie and I have added some thoughts in the document shared with us.

Below, we’re highlighting the mitigation measures, starting with the strongest ones (the ones that would really help us defend ourselves in a reclassification claim) and moving down to the alternative scenarios in case the previous ones are not possible/envisageable to implement in the short term (as we understand is the case):

*a) Putting in place processes allowing the fleet to block its drivers who are in breach of T&Cs, after this has been flagged by Bolt to the fleet* (in accordance with our T&Cs) - _this is the best legal solution, considering we only have an agreement with fleets and this would mean we are not at risk of meeting any ATD criteria._

*b) Blocking the entire fleet in case one of its drivers is in breach of T&Cs*. _We would recommend at least to look into putting in place a process allowing us to block fleets when several of their drivers are in breach. E.g. if a fleets receives safety events on more than 50% of their drivers._

*c)* If none of the first 2 options are developed, then it means Bolt is at risk of meeting several criteria - however, from an experience perspective, *properly informing the driver and its fleet* means that potentially we create less situations where drivers are unhappy and therefore we decrease the risks of drivers willing to sue us for reclassification - however ACT can always initiate claims and then a court would review all the facts, so such approach re: blocking might be held against us and be ruled by a court as fulfilling several criteria. In such case, we recommend that *all template communications that CS will use for hard block and investigative blocks are shared in a G-Doc with Legal so we may review them and advise on the best wording to decrease the risks associated with such approach*.

→ _High level advice_ is to ensure that:

* *the communication re blocking is clear, justified and references the correct provision(s) under our T&Cs;*
* *the communication re blocking is sent to both the fleet and the drive;*
* *the appeal system is clearly mentioned in the comm*.



*_3. Finally, regarding “Implementing a trigger for driver profile analysis”,_* can you please clarify if this profiling will be new in PT + if other countries have similar profiling processes? This raises *concerns from a Privacy perspective*, but before we involve our Privacy colleagues, we would need to understand better what are the changes in this respect.



Please let me know if you need further information or clarification.

Anton’s goals are:

Start using event_id, generated by our internal event_service to do event deduplication both for Facebook and Google (currently events are duplicated, since they are sent both through back- and frontend).

Currently we have the following infrastructure and possibilities for Apps:

# We are able to store Firebase id internally and send it to Google analytics (already exists: firebase_instance_id in ng_public.user_user)
# This Firebase id can be sent together with events (like first ride finished, regular ride finished). Those events can contain, for example, user LTV. Events and their values are accessible in GA.
# Every time the user receives his/her LTV calculation, we can send and event like 'user_ltv_calculated' having the value of LTV.



Possible idea for managing the quality of targeted users:

# Send the event ‘user_ltv_calculated' with the LTV of a user once it’s calculated for the first time to GA
# Create the audience in GA with best LTVs (top 50-30-10%)
# Possibly create look-a-likes for that audience to target users with better LTVs

Some limitations:

* this does not take to account that LTVs are updated weekly for each user (so might not work well for markets with unstable LTV predictions)



To build a prototype we need:

* create parquet file with firebase_user_id (+some other required parameters) and LTV predictions
* connect this parquet file to Rudderstack (asking Anton for access)
* Push the events as some 'user_ltv_calculated' to GA manually and make sure we see those in Google ads.

Hi Mirka!

I have added information about calculating the delay in both articles ([🥡 🥕 My courier is late / my courier is not moving|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/15239] and [🥡 🥕 Eater's order is delayed|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/89708]).

In [🥡 🥕 My courier is late / my courier is not moving|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/15239] we should cancel the order with Courier as the actor at fault if the order has been picked up, and I have added a note to cancel the order with Bolt as the actor at fault if the eater requests cancellation while the order is still being prepared by the Provider.

In the *🥡 🥕* [No courier is assigned to the order|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/29679], if no courier is assigned, we should cancel with Bolt at fault - I have added this to the article.

In the *🥡 🥕* [Eater's order is delayed|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/89708] if the courier causes the delay, it should be cancelled on the courier, if the provider causes the delay, it should be cancelled on the provider. I have added this to the article as well. 🙂 

Regarding swapping Step 1 and Step 2 - we have decided not to proceed with this change. While it does make sense, so does the current set up so we decided to keep it. It should not happen often that eaters complain about the courier not moving while they’re waiting at the restaurant - eaters can also see this in-app.

Regarding the links for the articles - we decided not to do this because we don’t want agents to switch through articles too much, additionally, if we link another process, then they’d have to start the process all over again in the linked article while the current steps are quite short even though they may contain duplicate info. It wouldn’t really save the agent’s time. 

Regarding *🥡 🥕* [No courier is assigned to the order|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/29679] we decided not to add this step about suggesting the eater contact us again because as you said, we don’t have a set time for this. We also shouldn’t let the eater know the order can be cancelled if the delay exceeds 30 minutes. So for now we will leave it like this, we haven’t received any complaints so far about this being problematic so it is possible that it doesn’t happen too often that no courier is assigned to the order after CS tries multiple times to assign one. Sometimes there isn’t a better solution other than adding supply. 🙂 

I have updated the non-existent article link in both [🥡🥕 Eater did not receive order|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/6429545509650] & [🥡🥕 🇨🇿 🇱🇻 🇷🇴 🇺🇦 Eater did not receive order|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/45315]. 

The broken image has been fixed. 

I have also rephrased the call attempts, you’re right about the wording!

Thank you again for all your suggestions and your patience, it is really appreciated. I’d suggest sending multiple separate SD tickets in the future though! 🙂 

I will close this ticket now but feel free to contact us if needed. 

Have a lovely day 💐 

Bina

I’m adding my thoughts here for the purposes of the wider project:

* *Compliance with European directives or regimes* - Has it been verified that package delivery services can be performed without being in breach of any European rules? No licence or authorisation needed? cc [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] 
* *Compliance with local rules*: PP/Reg team ([~accountid:60ec731b2f97d50069db1627] )should assess whether any local rules need to be complied with. 
** _e.g in MT, there’s an authorisation regime - not clear if authorisation is required from fleet operator or platform._ 
** _e.g. in PT, there’s a law and decrees about transportation of goods by road (IMT)._ 
* *T&Cs construction*: (cc [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] )
** +Mixing main RH terms with Delivery Services terms+: Even though Business sees this service as a plug-in service to RH (because it will be the same supply), the reality is that it is a service completely different from transportation of persons. _Example below with PT:_
*** _TVDE and Taxi services are regulated (and licenced) and should not be mischaracterized;_
*** _Delivery services cannot be provided during the course of a TVDE or Taxi service, and therefore the TVDE/Taxi operators and drivers at their service should be "off" TVDE/Taxi Transportation Services - which means that the vehicle used for the purpose of delivery services cannot be used under the perimeter of TVDE or Taxi._

→ It does not seem possible to add some additional specific Package Delivery Terms to the main TVDE or Taxi T&Cs. *We recommend having standalone terms for Package Delivery Services.*

It would also help in giving clarity to consumers (that they are using delivery services, not transporartyion services).

               +Mixing terms for Clients and Delivery Operators within the Delivery Services terms+: Clear information is required for consumers (consumer laws in West Europe are particularly strict). Further, this doesn’t follow the exiting approach at Bolt (we always have separate terms for users/riders/passengers and drivers/fleets).

→ *We recommend to have separate terms for Users* (most of them are expected to be consumers, not professionals) *and for Delievery Operators*. 

* *T&Cs content*: Several points TBD - some of the most important ones are Excluded Items and liability.



There are also *some concerns that should be discussed with local Ops team (cc* [~accountid:6257f823ed2b3e0074fd8114] *and* [~accountid:61124fbaec92ab0070270a0b] *):*

* TVDE Drivers will delivery Package Delivery Services through fleets HOWEVER the requirement to go through a fleet is only within the perimeters of TVDE laws, so they should be able to provide Package Delivery Services directly on their own → though this is probably not where we want to go, as this would also potentially increases the reclassification risks? BUT are fleet owners okay for Package Delivery Services to be performed by drivers under their account? cc [~accountid:60ec731b2f97d50069db1627] 
* Same question probably for taxi drivers under fleet?

{code:sql}  
SELECT city.name, count(etl_cases.id) as number_of_cases
FROM glue.ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case AS etl_cases
         LEFT JOIN glue.ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case_issue AS etl_issues
                   ON etl_cases.id = etl_issues.support_case_id
         LEFT JOIN glue.ng_customer_support.support_issue_store_support_issue AS issues
                   ON etl_issues.issue_key = issues.issue_key
         join glue.ng_public.admin_system_city city on city.id = etl_cases.city_id
WHERE
      etl_cases.created >= DATE '2023-06-01'
  AND etl_cases.created < DATE '2023-07-01'
  AND (etl_cases.state IS NULL OR etl_cases.state NOT IN ('draft', 'duplicate'))
  AND etl_cases.order_system = 'taxi'
  and issues.issue_title = 'My ride happened without me'
  group by city.name
  order by number_of_cases desc

Hey all, just adding my two cents here, if I may.

As Catarina mentioned, this is a service agreement and not an employment contract nor a temporary work usage contract, which means that all firing/hiring/disciplinary decisions are done by Randstad, with Bolt providing orientations for that. 

By default, the orientations should be the same as usual for Randstad, but we also don’t know what sort of contracts Randstad has with the pickers, and legally they don’t have to share them with us, so we don’t know exactly what’s implied in terms of liabilities for Randstad/Bolt. 

Can the employee complain to ACT? Totally, and to CITE as well (Comissão para a Igualdade no Trabalho e no Emprego) - being a mother during breastfeeding period, she cannot be dismissed based simply on the fact that she’s a mother breastfeeding. Any dismissal for people in this situation, whether with just cause or not, needs to be communicated beforehand to CITE and they need to approve such termination. If not approved, then the company would need to go to court to revert the decision. If the court decides that there’s not enough proof to justify the dismissal (and again, for people in this situation, is extremely likely that that’s the case), then there are no grounds for dismissal from Randstad’s side. 
Can they reassign her to other projects/clients that they have? Again, this on Randstad’s to review and decide based on the contract they have with her.

I know it’s not much help, but it’s important that you’re aware that this is not a regular case based on the legal protections that pregnant women and women breastfeeding have.

Hi,

following our previous meeting and a potential inconsistency with DLA’s advice provided in 2021, we have agreed to clarify this point again with the outside attorney to ensure we are all aligned. 

DLA has confirmed that there is no legal requirement to confirm repute of the taxi driver and hence no legal requirement for onboarding of taxi drivers operating in Bolt Platform with a taxi (not a vehicle uncharacterised). The TVDE law does not apply in such case.

Therefore, *there is no legal obligation determining Bolt to require criminal records from taxi drivers (in the onboarding and during the time the taxi driver is registered in the app).* 

Please let me know if you need any further information or clarification. Below you can find the full advice of DLA.

__________________________

+QUESTION BOLT:+ It would appear that for the case of taxi drivers operating with a taxi (and not vehicles uncharacterised) we would require to following documents during onboarding: taxi licence (i.e. "alvara"), certificate of car registration (i.e. "documento único automóvel"), taxi driver certificate and driving licence. Could you please confirm the understanding above is correct? 

_DLA Piper 2: Yes. Our assumption for the previous advice was that taxi drivers would be operating with a TVDE vehicle. Provided that taxi drivers are operating with taxis, the TVDE Driver certificate shall not be required._

+QUESTION BOLT:+ Additionally, in light of the above could you please confirm that a criminal record is not a requirement for onboarding of taxi drivers operating in Bolt Platform with a taxi (not a vehicle uncharacterised)? 

_DLA Piper 2: In such case, considering that the platform is not subject to a legal requirement to confirm if requirements for the exercise of the transportation service are met,_ *_there is no legal requirement to confirm repute of the taxi driver_*_, so there is no legal requirement for onboarding of taxi drivers operating in Bolt Platform with a taxi (not a vehicle uncharacterised).”_

Only addition is: we've added photo capture config under each photo: When photo_capture config is provided in treatment group we need to ensure that the number of photos listed in the config is really taken and uploaded to verification DB and accessible/visible on verification flow run page along with it's associated capture config. Resolution provided should be respected (however resulting photo might be a bit lower or higher resolution, check [here](https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4427122192/Capture+Configs+Mobile+Perspective)). Performance when making series of photos should be acceptable. Uploads should be quick and should not block user for longer than time of uploading a single photo as it used to be. Flashlight logic is also changed (more info [here](https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4427122192/Capture+Configs+Mobile+Perspective#Parameters-one-by-one)): long story short: when flashlight is provided in capture config we hide button on camera screen. If not provided we keep default behaviour and let user decide whether to use flashlight or not. Added ui element: when uploading camera shot button is disabled and indeterminate progress added for 'work' indication.

# At search time, a mapping is stored in Redis, with key = user id and value = all etas of all providers that the client sees on the home categories screen. Only the home categories call is used, as it contains all providers that the client can choose from, and we are also interested in the original search ETAs seen by the client, which lead to conversion.
## Call graph here with the home categories call done by delivery-provider-search: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~235697389/pages/4400513293/Call+graph+delivery-provider-search+-+internal+computeEtaAtProviderSearch|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~235697389/pages/4400513293/Call+graph+delivery-provider-search+-+internal+computeEtaAtProviderSearch|smart-link] 

2. At checkout time, the mapping is retrieved from Redis and stored into the eta table in the DB. If the mapping is not found, the basket will be left without a search row, as just doing a fake search call would defeat the purpose of saving only the ETAs seen by the client originally, and these can change in time.

Hey!

Noted! Generally, I see no objections, but the following must be followed:

# With respect to pre-judicial collection proceedings the order can only be cancelled by the client if *a term of notice of three months is observed*. The cancellation must be *in written form*. In this case the customer owes the fees, expenses and commissions incurred. With respect to monitoring proceedings the order can only be cancelled for the first time after the end of the second year. The cancellation must be in written form and needs a term of notice of three months. In this case the customer owes the fees and expenses incurred as well as – in case of preceding pre-judicial collection proceedings – the fees and expenses incurred which have not been compensated by debtor's payments.
# *The claim for commission remains even if the debtor meets with the obligations only after the expiration of the term of notice*, as far as measures of the International Debt Collection Department have been concurrently causative for the payment.
# As long as the order is valid, *the creditor is not entitled to continue himself handling the claim or having it handled by any other institution* (collecting agent, representative). In case of non-observance of these conditions, particularly, if the creditor releases the claim or compounds with the debtor without the agreement of the International Debt Collection Department, the commission calculated on the volume of the total order becomes due. The claim of commission becomes also due if the creditor takes back the goods, or if another compensation is arranged for. Such an arrangement does not afflict the claim of reimbursement of all expenses involved.

* Yes, my team does the promoting and possesses the know-how

following our previous meeting and a potential inconsistency with DLA’s advice provided in 2021, we have agreed to clarify this point again with the outside attorney to ensure we are all aligned.

DLA has confirmed that there is no legal requirement to confirm repute of the taxi driver and hence no legal requirement for onboarding of taxi drivers operating in Bolt Platform with a taxi (not a vehicle uncharacterised). The TVDE law does not apply in such case.

Therefore, *there is no legal obligation determining Bolt to require criminal records from taxi drivers (in the onboarding and during the time the taxi driver is registered in the app).*

Please let me know if you need any further information or clarification. Below you can find the full advice of DLA.

__________________________

+QUESTION BOLT:+ It would appear that for the case of taxi drivers operating with a taxi (and not vehicles uncharacterised) we would require to following documents during onboarding: taxi licence (i.e. "alvara"), certificate of car registration (i.e. "documento único automóvel"), taxi driver certificate and driving licence. Could you please confirm the understanding above is correct?

_DLA Piper 2: Yes. Our assumption for the previous advice was that taxi drivers would be operating with a TVDE vehicle. Provided that taxi drivers are operating with taxis, the TVDE Driver certificate shall not be required._

+QUESTION BOLT:+ Additionally, in light of the above could you please confirm that a criminal record is not a requirement for onboarding of taxi drivers operating in Bolt Platform with a taxi (not a vehicle uncharacterised)?

_DLA Piper 2: In such case, considering that the platform is not subject to a legal requirement to confirm if requirements for the exercise of the transportation service are met,_ *_there is no legal requirement to confirm repute of the taxi driver_*_, so there is no legal requirement for onboarding of taxi drivers operating in Bolt Platform with a taxi (not a vehicle uncharacterised).”_

In the end what we want is to be able to look at the specific auto-acceptance rule evaluation result and figure out what went wrong. At the moment we don't really care how would we do it. There are three possibilities:

# If the rule fails simply render the evaluation result in the log
Upsides:
#* The implementation is trivial, so we get no new code
#* The mismatched data is explicitly stored in the condition arguments, so one can immediately figure out why a certain comparison failed
# Downsides:
#* Kibana logs is not the best way to debug things
#* We expose personal data to the logs
# If the specific condition fails we log the comparison-specific config
Upsides:
#* Easy to implement
# Donwsides:
#* Kibana logs is not the best way to debug things + we potentially write multiple messages per document
# If the result fails we traverse the config, collect the individual comparisons, render decision reason and store it in the db
Upsides:
#* Uses the existing interface
# Downsides:
#* Requires a bit of coding

I am leaning towards option #3. It's a bit more code, but it's miles better when it comes to user experience.

h2. *Feedback from Team Leads*

*Lithuania*

* CSAT is higher than in other markets because agents are calling the drivers instead of writing them a message. First, they check if the driver doesn’t have an ongoing trip and if not, they call them. They usually try to call the driver 3 times; if they don’t pick up, they send an outgoing message. According to Martyna, if the driver doesn’t have an ongoing trip and is at work, they pick up the phone in most cases.
* The current process only says to contact the driver but it doesn’t specify how, the updated process will follow LT example.

*Estonia*

* There are a few reasons why CSAT is high in EE for lost item cases. One is that CS calls drivers in lost item cases instead of sending a message, which again aligns with the findings from the LT market.
* Other reasons are that Tallinn is a small city, distances are not that big, which makes it easier to arrange an item drop-off. Additionally, drivers are experienced so it’s not common for them to decline giving an item back. 

*Norway*

* [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NOCS/pages/4346053947/Deep+dive+into+the+ATIs+I+lost+an+item+I+lost+my+phone+from+January+2023+for|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NOCS/pages/4346053947/Deep+dive+into+the+ATIs+I+lost+an+item+I+lost+my+phone+from+January+2023+for|smart-link] 
* In the deep dive, there were only 3 cases where CS escalated the case to Ops who contacted the FO and all of these cases were resolved (not sure if the item was retrieved though).

*Spain*

* *Why is AHT so high:*
** We used to have a lot of cases getting escalated on social media + cases escalated to Ops directly, so we adapted the process and started _calling D and FO,_ in addition to sending them outgoing messages. Some larger Fleets even have a dedicated 24/7 phone line just for lost items.
** With the [deep dive|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1p4g5ly1cR0354fFJ2PUqygu9QsnicQsv9ehHo-wpKT0/edit?usp=sharing] it seems like it's not worth calling any of them actually , and I see that OS only called FOs in 25% of cases. It might be connected to the fact that they can't call during the weekends, and then they forget.
** *July 23:* 36% item was not found, 33% item was found, 14% user contacted about somebody else's ride, 7% no reply received from D/FO
* *In-house AHT:*
** We have a specific workflow for *high-value items* (laptops, keys, important documents). If OS don't receive a reply from D/FO after 3 days, they escalate to tier 2, who then escalate it via Slack and tag relevant Ops member who is responsible for the exact city. Ops contacts the FO and gets a reply from them.
** 99% success rate in getting a reply from the FO about the item this way
** In June-July 2023 only 25 cases were escalated to Ops, in 28% of these escalated cases the item was found. Deep dive [here|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/19z43sav_sxoPpjLRq4jh8-QOKF6ia-HSRo1Na5IAenA/edit?usp=sharing].
** Why don't FOs answer CS, but answer Ops? Possible reason: CS have a robotic 7 second-long message in English at the start of every outgoing call, stating that the call is being recorded for quality and training purposes. Spaniards often don't speak English, so they hang up when they hear it.
** Product are fixing the language issue, escalated [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C032D4ZGZR6/p1690463852325459].

*Germany*

* Awaiting feedback (no response from TL, followed up on August 7).

*Partner markets*

* *Georgia*: call the driver & follow the global process
* *Austria:* call the driver, if they don’t respond, block them sometimes‼️ 
* *Saudi Arabia:* first send an outgoing case > if no response, call the driver > if no response, block the account ‼️, compensate the driver with 30 SAR if they give back the item to the rider
* *Hungary:* follow the global process, drivers can also leave lost item at the hub

*Azerbaijan*

* Awaiting feedback (TL is off)

I selected 1 order in live which is delayed much more than buffered deadline and checked all the logs related to order {{1330467899}} . Following is the sequence of events happened. (Time in GMT)

1. {{10:44:51}} Order is created and Buffering deadline is set as {{10:45:07}} (i.e., ~15 seconds)
2. {{10:44:53}} First time order picked by GroupingWorker and it updates the wait_until as {{10:45:03}}
3. But groupingWorker doesn’t send this order for matching because when it does grouping, it does not find any {{not_buffered}} or {{buffered_expired}} at that point of time, hence it returns from line#37 in the splitIntoGroups method. (screenshot attached)
4. {{10:45:03}} Now this order is picked again by GroupingWorker along with 2 other orders {{1330468006, 1330468018}} and it updates wait_until as {{10:45:13}}
5. The same thing mentioned in point 3 above happens again for all 3 orders.
6. {{10:45:13}} All three orders (i.e., {{1330467899, 1330468006, 1330468018}}) are picked again by GroupingWorker along with another order {{1330468114}} and since now the buffering deadline of first order is expired, it fill the rest of group with all other 4 orders and send for matching.
7. Now we see that the order was matched at {{10:45:13}} while the buffering deadline was {{10:45:07}}. 6 seconds delay after buffering deadline expired.

Diagnosis results:
1. {{wait_until}} intervened with buffering deadline even before first matching round.
2. Update wait_until of only those orders which are grouped for matching.
3. I feel the logic of {{splitIntoGroups}} is correct. It should NOT send {{buffered_not_expired}} orders for matching if there are no {{not_buffered}} or {{buffered_expired}} available.

As per logs, message scheduler is working fine.

{noformat}with final_order_tries as (
    select
        id,
        state,
        city_id,
        driver_city_id,
        driver_id,
        order_id,
        driver_app_version
    from ng_public.company_order_try
    where company_order_try.created_date in (date '2023-07-20')
      and company_order_try.city_id = 25
      and company_order_try.retry_to_try is NULL
      and company_order_try.driver_city_id = company_order_try.city_id
),
     extended_try_logs as (
         select
             final_order_tries.driver_id,
             final_order_tries.order_id,
             final_order_tries.city_id,
             final_order_tries.driver_city_id,
             final_order_tries.driver_app_version,
             log.order_try_id,
             log.to_state as state,
             log.created as state_start,
             LEAD(log.created) OVER (partition by log.city_id, log.order_try_id order by created) as state_end,
                 MIN(log.created) over (partition by log.city_id, log.order_try_id) as order_try_start,
                 MAX(log.created) over (partition by log.city_id, log.order_try_id) as order_try_end,
                 final_order_tries.state as final_state
         from ng_public.company_order_try_state_log log
                  inner join final_order_tries
                             on log.order_try_id = final_order_tries.id
                                 and log.city_id = final_order_tries.city_id
         where log.created_date in (date '2023-07-20')
           and log.city_id = 25
     ),
     location_speeds as (
         select
             case 
                 WHEN location.gps_speed_mps is null THEN true
                 else false
                 end as is_speed_null,
             log.driver_app_version
         from geo__tracking_live.tracking_driver_locations_sqs location
        -- left join extended_try_logs log on location.entity_id = log.driver_id
        inner join extended_try_logs log on location.entity_id = log.driver_id
             and location.server_time >= log.state_start and location.server_time < log.state_end
             and location.city_id = log.city_id
         where location.created_at_date in (date '2023-07-20')
            and location.city_id = 25
    )
select
    driver_app_version, is_speed_null, count(*)
from location_speeds
group by driver_app_version, is_speed_null;{noformat}

{noformat}day_of_week_idx, day_of_week = df["day_of_week"].factorize(sort=True)
date = df["date_day"].to_numpy()

coords = {

}

with pm.Model(coords=coords) as model:
    
    #target = pm.MutableData(name="target", value=df[f'{target_variable}'])
    ftr_andr = pm.MutableData(name="ftr_andr", value=df['ftr_cohort_14days_android'])
    ftr_ios = pm.MutableData(name="ftr_ios", value=df['ftr_cohort_14days_ios'])

    costs_android = pm.MutableData(name="costs_android", value=df['costs_android'])
    costs_ios = pm.MutableData(name="costs_ios", value=df['costs_ios'])
    
    general_trend = pm.Normal(name="alpha_trend", mu=150, sigma=200)
    intercept_andr = pm.Normal(name="intercept_andr", mu=0, sigma=200)
    intercept_ios = pm.Normal(name="intercept_ios", mu=0, sigma=200)

    beta_spend_android = pm.HalfNormal(name="beta_spend_android", sigma=200)
    beta_spend_ios = pm.HalfNormal(name="beta_spend_ios", sigma=200)
    
    trend = pm.MutableData(name="trend", value=df['trend'])

    #b_day_of_week = pm.ZeroSumNormal(name="b_day_of_week_", sigma=1, dims="day_of_week")

    #mu_var = intercept + alpha_trend*trend# +  sum(contrib.values()) + alpha_discounts*discounts
    mu_andr = pm.Deterministic(name="mu_andr", var= intercept_andr + trend*general_trend + beta_spend_android*costs_android )
    mu_ios = pm.Deterministic(name="mu_ios", var=intercept_ios + trend*general_trend + beta_spend_ios*costs_ios )

    sigma = pm.HalfNormal(name="sigma", sigma=200)

    pm.Normal(name="l_andr", mu=mu_andr, sigma=sigma, observed=ftr_andr)
    pm.Normal(name="l_ios", mu=mu_ios, sigma=sigma, observed=ftr_ios){noformat}

*Model that I used to predict iOS*

{noformat}day_of_week_idx, day_of_week = df["day_of_week"].factorize(sort=True)
date = df["date_day"].to_numpy()

coords = {
    "day_of_week": day_of_week,
    "date" :date
}

with pm.Model(coords=coords) as model_to_fix_ios:
    
    #target = pm.MutableData(name="target", value=df[f'{target_variable}'])
    ftr_andr = pm.MutableData(name="ftr_andr", value=df['ftr_cohort_14days_android'])
    ftr_ios = pm.MutableData(name="ftr_ios", value=df['ftr_cohort_14days_ios'])

    costs_android = pm.MutableData(name="costs_android", value=df['costs_android'])
    costs_ios = pm.MutableData(name="costs_ios", value=df['costs_ios'])
    
    general_trend = pm.Normal(name="general_trend", mu=150, sigma=200)
    intercept_andr = pm.Normal(name="intercept_andr", mu=0, sigma=200)
    intercept_ios = pm.Normal(name="intercept_ios", mu=0, sigma=200)

    beta_spend_android = pm.HalfNormal(name="beta_spend_android", sigma=200)
    beta_spend_ios = pm.HalfNormal(name="beta_spend_ios", sigma=200)
    
    trend = pm.MutableData(name="trend", value=df['trend'])

    b_day_of_week = pm.ZeroSumNormal(name="b_day_of_week", sigma=100, dims="day_of_week")
    day_of_week = pm.MutableData(name="day_of_week", value=df['day_of_week'])

    #mu_var = intercept + alpha_trend*trend# +  sum(contrib.values()) + alpha_discounts*discounts
    mu_andr = pm.Deterministic(name="mu_andr", var=intercept_andr + trend*general_trend + beta_spend_android*costs_android + b_day_of_week[day_of_week_idx]*day_of_week)
    mu_ios = pm.Deterministic(name="mu_ios", var=intercept_ios + trend*general_trend + beta_spend_ios*costs_ios + b_day_of_week[day_of_week_idx]*day_of_week)

    sigma = pm.HalfNormal(name="sigma", sigma=200)

    pm.Normal(name="l_andr", mu=mu_andr, sigma=sigma, observed=ftr_andr)
    pm.Normal(name="l_ios", mu=mu_ios, sigma=sigma, observed=ftr_ios){noformat}

    general_trend = pm.Normal(name="general_trend", mu=150, sigma=200)
    intercept_andr = pm.Normal(name="intercept_andr", mu=0, sigma=200)
    intercept_ios = pm.Normal(name="intercept_ios", mu=0, sigma=200)

    beta_spend_android = pm.HalfNormal(name="beta_spend_android", sigma=200)
    beta_spend_ios = pm.HalfNormal(name="beta_spend_ios", sigma=200)
    
    trend = pm.MutableData(name="trend", value=df['trend'])

    sigma_slopes = pm.Exponential(name="sigma_slope", lam=20)
    slopes = pm.GaussianRandomWalk(
        name="slopes",
        sigma=sigma_slopes,
        init_dist=Exponential.dist(lam=1 / 0.1),
        dims="date",
    )

    b_day_of_week = pm.ZeroSumNormal(name="b_day_of_week", sigma=100, dims="day_of_week")
    day_of_week = pm.MutableData(name="day_of_week", value=df['day_of_week'])

    #mu_var = intercept + alpha_trend*trend# +  sum(contrib.values()) + alpha_discounts*discounts
    mu_andr = pm.Deterministic(name="mu_andr", var=intercept_andr + trend*general_trend + slopes*costs_android + b_day_of_week[day_of_week_idx]*day_of_week)
    mu_ios = pm.Deterministic(name="mu_ios", var=intercept_ios + trend*general_trend + slopes*costs_ios + b_day_of_week[day_of_week_idx]*day_of_week)

    sigma = pm.HalfNormal(name="sigma", sigma=200)

    pm.Normal(name="l_andr", mu=mu_andr, sigma=sigma, observed=ftr_andr)
    pm.Normal(name="l_ios", mu=mu_ios, sigma=sigma, observed=ftr_ios)
{noformat}

*Lease Agreement between Bolt & Regus:*

Although the agreement does not explicitly state Bolt's right to terminate voluntarily, it outlines the circumstances under which payment of the lump sum, which would have been due upon termination for the remaining term, becomes applicable. These circumstances include where the landlord terminates on account of the following: 

# If Bolt becomes insolvent or declares bankruptcy.
# If Bolt breaches any of its obligations and fails to rectify the breach within 14 days after receiving notice.
# If Bolt engages in conduct that is incompatible with ordinary office use.
# If Bolt's conduct continues despite being notified, or if the conduct is significant enough to warrant termination.
# If Bolt is in violation of the compliance law clause mentioned below.

Based on the above conditions detailed in clause 1.8, two arguments may be inferred:

a. that the lump sum payment would only be applicable if termination occurs due to the grounds mentioned. If termination is based on any reason other than those highlighted above, the lump sum payment would not be applicable. 

b. since the agreement does not expressly grant Bolt the right to voluntarily terminate the lease, then Bolt may be strictly prohibited from terminating the agreement before the expiration of the term. 

Our recommendation:

The agreement only provides for two modes of termination: (i) termination by effluxion of time, and (ii) termination without notice by the landlord based on the specified grounds.

While it might be a stretch, we can argue under point (a) that termination by Bolt in this instance (even though not contemplated under the agreement) does not fall within the circumstances detailed in clause 1.8 of the agreement, and thus the lump sum payment should not be applicable.

Relatedly, we note that the agreement is yet to be signed. [~accountid:63e3ef2dbf837c6893db58e3] please confirm if this agreement is already in force.

*Lease Agreement between Urban Office v Bolt*

The termination clause of this agreement does not contemplate the payment of a lump sum to cover the unutilized portion of the term, if the agreement is terminated prematurely.  All that is required of Bolt in the event of termination are - 

i. peacefully give vacant possession of the premises in an acceptable state of repair; 

ii. hand over the keys, access card and all equipment belonging to the landlord; and

ii. payment of a maximum fee of one month value of rent, for administrative and office costs related to the termination of the agreement.

We note that this agreement is effective for 36 months - from 21 March 2022 to 20 March 2025. However, should Bolt intend to terminate now, we will not be mandated to pay rent for the unutilized portion of the term.

Hi [~accountid:614c2822be1de8006be956c4] , 

I understand that Ops would like to implement a new Courier Performance Control using Matching Policies and is envisaging to perform a test during a couple of weeks with around 10 couriers. The aim is to prioritize best performing couriers without blocking couriers and overall to ensure quality of delivery service. The process would consist in:

* Having weekly performance reviews of couriers on a city level where they are ranked based on quality metrics;
* Setting up prioritization of couriers (Admin).

However, as discussed before, the envisaged prioritization might be seen as fulfilling criteria 2, 3, 4 and/or 5 of the ATD Law.  Moreover, I would like to point out further concerns with this new feature:

* Performance control through quality metrics is typical for an employer vs employee relation. Therefore, it is recommended to avoid language such as performance or control and instead concentrate in quality of service and prioritization.
* Even though this new feature would not provide any external visibility into how the order allocation is done, it is likely that some couriers may face significant drops in their number of orders and consequently be dissatisfied. This may result in complaints and questions addressed to Bolt and potentially some court cases, which we are starting  to increasingly see in Portugal.
* If Bolt is asked to clarify how the order allocation logic works in court, the prioritization logic will likely be disclosed and assessed. Bolt might be also requested to provide details regarding the algorithm, which we are starting to see in other jurisdictions (e.g. the UK). 

While it seems very difficult not to control or supervise the activity of the couriers, it is important to remember DLA’s advice that often the only way to avoid meeting the reclassification criteria is to go through the fleet, that is, to involve the fleet. This involvement would appear not to be foreseen in this new feature. Hence, while Legal can advise on the wording to be used for this project and communications with potential dissatisfied couriers, there is no particular way to avoid reclassification risks in this new feature. 

Should you still decide to go ahead with this new feature, I would suggest to consider the following mitigation measures:

# Putting in place processes allowing the fleet to block its couriers who received client’s complaints and are in breach of T&Cs. We could inform the fleet that a client complained about this courier and request the fleet do something to address this issue. If the fleet doesn't do anything then, Bolt should envisage imposing a penalty first, and then could potentially block the fleet (not the courier) after a few events if the fleet hasn’t done anything. Blocking the courier if the fleet doesn't do it would be very risky. This mitigation measure has been specifically mentioned by DLA for RH.
# Considering the involvement of clients, providing transparency to both clients and couriers of this feature and, additionally, focusing the project on prioritization for quality assurance purposes. My understanding is that this is the option followed by RH. However, as I noted in our last discussion, the risk level for RH is arguably lower given, among others, the application of the TVDE law, which does not apply to your vertical. I suggest to involve [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] on this point, in particular, once she is back from her leave since she has much more background than myself on this particular matter.

Please let me have your thoughts and questions. I am happy to further discuss.

Thank you.
