Templare for Query

**

{noformat}{{
  config(
    schema="ng_public_spark",
    materialized="incremental",
    incremental_strategy="merge",
    unique_key=["master_user_id"],
    partition_by="activation_date",
    on_schema_change='sync_all_columns'
  )
}}

WITH global_multipliers AS (
      -- calculates global average multipliers per each number of days left in lifetime

	SELECT
	lifetime_1y_days_left,
    -- GMV multiplier
    AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur) AS lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur_avg,
    COALESCE(AVG(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur),0) AS lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_avg,
    (AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur)+COALESCE(AVG(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur),0))/CAST(AVG(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur) AS REAL) AS flv_gmv_eur_multiplier
    FROM {{source("ng_public_spark","eater_lifetime_ltv")}} 
    WHERE lifetime_1y_days_left IS NOT null
    AND computed_on = (SELECT max(computed_on) FROM {{source("ng_public_spark","eater_lifetime_ltv")}})
    GROUP BY 1
      ),
      
eater_ltv_adjusted AS (
    -- -- temporary solution for model's collapse on new cities
    -- -- Read more here https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/MARTD-232 and here https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/DS-2348
SELECT
      l.city_id,
      l.user_id,
      l.lifetime_1y_days_left,
      mm.gmv_model_accuracy,
      l.computed_on,
      l.lifetime_1y_start_date,
      l.lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur,
      l.lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur,
      COALESCE(l.lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur,0) AS lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur_old,
      COALESCE(l.lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur * gm.flv_gmv_eur_multiplier, l.lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur) AS lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur_new,
      COALESCE(
              COALESCE(l.lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur * gm.flv_gmv_eur_multiplier, l.lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur)
              - l.lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur, l.lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur)  AS lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_new
    FROM {{source("ng_public_spark","eater_lifetime_ltv")}} l
    LEFT JOIN {{source("ng_public_spark","eater_lifetime_flv_model_metrics")}} mm ON mm.city_id = l.city_id
        AND mm.computed_on = l.computed_on
    LEFT JOIN global_multipliers gm ON l.lifetime_1y_days_left = gm.lifetime_1y_days_left
        AND mm.gmv_model_accuracy = 'immeasurable' -- only apply multipliers if model accuracy is immeasurable
        AND l.lifetime_1y_days_left IS NOT NULL  -- disregard multipliers for riders with 1y history
    WHERE l.computed_on = (select max(computed_on) from {{source("ng_public_spark","eater_lifetime_ltv")}})
    )
    
SELECT
	ltv_predictions.user_id as master_user_id
	,DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) AS activation_date
	,ltv_predictions.computed_on AS date_compute
	,MIN(CASE
		WHEN DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) < DATE '2016-01-01' THEN 0 -- we don't have GMV data for old cohorts
		WHEN city_metrics.gmv_model_used = TRUE OR (DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) < DATE_ADD(current_date(),-365) -- THEN 'full LTV results for cities'
		AND DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) >= DATE '2016-01-01') THEN 1
		ELSE 0 END) AS full_gmv_available_flag
	,COUNT(distinct ltv_predictions.city_id) AS cities
	,SUM(lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur_old) AS lifetime_1y_ltv_gmv_eur_old
	,SUM(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur) AS lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur
  ,SUM(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_new) AS lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur
  ,SUM(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur*COALESCE(CAST(pc.value  AS DECIMAL(4,3)),0.11)) AS lifetime_1y_hlv_profit_simplified_eur
  ,SUM(lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur_new*COALESCE(CAST(pc.value  AS DECIMAL(4,3)),0.11)) AS lifetime_1y_flv_profit_simplified_eur
  ,current_timestamp() as _last_ingested
FROM eater_ltv_adjusted AS ltv_predictions
LEFT JOIN {{source("ng_public_spark","eater_lifetime_flv_model_metrics")}} AS city_metrics
ON city_metrics.city_id = ltv_predictions.city_id AND city_metrics.computed_on = ltv_predictions.computed_on
LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_public_spark", "admin_system_city") }}  AS city ON ltv_predictions.city_id = city.id
LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_public_spark", "admin_system_country") }} AS country ON city.country_code = country.code
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
    Distinct DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) AS activation_date_mapper,
    country.code AS country_mapper,
    MAX(Date(pc.month_applied)) AS profitability_date_mapper
    FROM {{ source("ng_public_spark", "eater_lifetime_ltv") }} AS ltv_predictions
    LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_public_spark", "admin_system_city") }} AS city ON ltv_predictions.city_id = city.id
    LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_public_spark", "admin_system_country") }} AS country ON city.country_code = country.code
    LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing_spark", "delivery_profit_rates") }} AS pc
    ON pc.country_code = country.code AND DATE(ltv_predictions.lifetime_1y_start_date)>=date(pc.month_applied) AND variable = 'Profit'
    GROUP BY 1,2
) AS dates_mapper ON dates_mapper.activation_date_mapper = DATE(lifetime_1y_start_date) AND dates_mapper.country_mapper = country.code
LEFT JOIN {{ source("ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing_spark", "delivery_profit_rates") }} AS pc ON dates_mapper.profitability_date_mapper = Date(pc.month_applied) AND dates_mapper.country_mapper=pc.country_code

WHERE lifetime_1y_days_left is not null
GROUP BY 1,2,3{noformat}

{code:sql}WITH abusers AS (
SELECT 
k.driver_id AS driver_id,
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.ng_touting = 1 THEN k.orders END) AS offline_rides,
COUNT (DISTINCT k.orders) AS all_orders,
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.ng_touting = 1 THEN k.orders END)*1.00/COUNT (DISTINCT k.orders) AS touting_ratio
FROM (
WITH api AS (
SELECT 
d.meta.order_id AS order_id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
CAST(get_json_object(d.input, '$.data.prediction_info.distance_in_meters')AS double) AS predicted_distance,
CAST(get_json_object(d.input, '$.data.actual_info.distance_in_meters')AS double) AS actual_distance,
CAST(get_json_object(d.input, '$.data.driver_location.driving_with_client.lat')AS double) AS driving_with_client_lat,
CAST(get_json_object(d.input, '$.data.driver_location.driving_with_client.lng')AS double) AS driving_with_client_lng,
CAST(get_json_object(d.input, '$.data.driver_location.arrived_to_destination.lat')AS double) AS arrived_to_destination_lat,
CAST(get_json_object(d.input, '$.data.driver_location.arrived_to_destination.lng')AS double) AS arrived_to_destination_lng
FROM 
archive_analytical.driver_overcharge_check AS d
WHERE 
d.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND d.created_hour >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND d.meta.country = 'ng' 
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
)
SELECT
etl.order_id AS orders,	
ot.driver_id AS driver_id,
CASE WHEN i.predicted_distance > i.actual_distance and 
ROUND((111.111 *
    DEGREES(ACOS(LEAST(1.0, COS(RADIANS(i.arrived_to_destination_lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(co.destination_lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(i.arrived_to_destination_lng - co.destination_lng))
         + SIN(RADIANS(i.arrived_to_destination_lat))
         * SIN(RADIANS(co.destination_lat))))))*1000) > 2000 AND (ROUND((111.111 *
    DEGREES(ACOS(LEAST(1.0, COS(RADIANS(co.lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(i.arrived_to_destination_lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(co.lng - i.arrived_to_destination_lng))
         + SIN(RADIANS(co.lat))
         * SIN(RADIANS(i.arrived_to_destination_lat))))))*1000)/ROUND((111.111 *
    DEGREES(ACOS(LEAST(1.0, COS(RADIANS(co.destination_lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(i.driving_with_client_lat))
         * COS(RADIANS(co.destination_lng - i.driving_with_client_lng))
         + SIN(RADIANS(co.destination_lat))
         * SIN(RADIANS(i.driving_with_client_lat))))))*1000) < 0.3) 
THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS ng_touting
FROM 
ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order AS co ON etl.order_id = co.id AND etl.city_id = co.city_id 
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try ot ON etl.order_id = ot.order_id AND etl.city_id = ot.city_id 
LEFT JOIN api AS i ON i.order_id = etl.order_id AND i.user_id = etl.user_id -- i.calculation_id = etl.fraud_calculation_id
WHERE 
etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND co.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
AND etl.order_type = 'rides'
AND etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
AND ot.state = 'finished'
AND etl.country_code = 'ng' 
GROUP BY 1,2,3
) AS k 
GROUP BY 1 
HAVING 		
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.ng_touting = 1 THEN k.orders END) > 5 
AND 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN k.ng_touting = 1 THEN k.orders END)*1.00/COUNT (DISTINCT k.orders) > 0.6
ORDER BY 4 DESC 
),
api AS (
SELECT 
d.meta.order_id AS order_id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
CAST(get_json_object(d.input, '$.data.prediction_info.distance_in_meters')AS double) AS predicted_distance,
CAST(get_json_object(d.input, '$.data.actual_info.distance_in_meters')AS double) AS actual_distance,
CAST(get_json_object(d.input, '$.data.driver_location.driving_with_client.lat')AS double) AS driving_with_client_lat,
CAST(get_json_object(d.input, '$.data.driver_location.driving_with_client.lng')AS double) AS driving_with_client_lng,
CAST(get_json_object(d.input, '$.data.driver_location.arrived_to_destination.lat')AS double) AS arrived_to_destination_lat,
CAST(get_json_object(d.input, '$.data.driver_location.arrived_to_destination.lng')AS double) AS arrived_to_destination_lng
FROM 
archive_analytical.driver_overcharge_check AS d
WHERE 
d.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)

Real Decreto 933/2021 (RD 933) provides for a huge list of information that must be mandatorily provided to the Spanish Ministry of Defence (MoD) about (i) the company supplying car-sharing services, (ii) the lessee of the car, (iii) the main driver and the secondary driver – if there is one -, and (iv) each transaction carried out.

However, from my POV, the most relevant topic that arises from these Regulations that should be analyzed is *who is liable to provide such information to the Spanish MoD*

(Pls note that this topic is related to question 3 raised by [~accountid:625fb4921046bb0071ddf448]).

In accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 2 (Definitions) of the RD 933, car-sharing activities are defined as those _“carried out in order to supply the use of a car without a driver to third parties, for a specified time, in exchange for consideration or price._ +_In all cases_+_, the following activities_ +_fall within the scope of the definition_+_:_

_a)             Car rental activities carried out by companies providing these services._

_b)             […]_

_c)             The activity of_ +_digital platforms_+ _that provide, for compensation or for free,_ +_online intermediation services_+_, either if they perform as the principal supplier of the underlying (car-sharing) service or not, as long as they provide (online intermediation) services in Spain.”_

Under the provision above, I think that both Zity (as the principal car-sharing service provider) and Bolt Ops OÜ (as the principal online intermediation services provider) *might be both liable to provide the Spanish MoD with the users’ information*.

Therefore, on the basis of the provision above, I think it may be worthwhile analyzing, from the legal perspective, the following options for the partnership with Zity:

# If Bolt merely performs as an *online intermediation services provider* (like in our regular RH business model), Zity may claim that it is liable to provide the Spanish MoD with the users' information under letter a) of Article 2.2, but perhaps we can assume the liability to provide the Spanish MoD with the users’ information, on the basis of letter c) of Article 2.2. of the RD, via the Partnership Agreement with Zity. This way, we would avoid furnishing Zity with the users’ information, as Bolt would be liable to comply with such an obligation.
# If we agree to set up a *reseller business model* with Zity (where Zity sells car-sharing services to Bolt and Bolt resells car-sharing services to Spanish end-users) I think that Bolt will the solely liable to provide the Spanish MoD with the users’ information.

Naturally, the implications (legal, tax, billing, commerce, finance and accounting, etc) arising from each one of the two afore-listed business models would have to be analyzed separately.

Thank you and have a good day.

As the drivers are not employees of Bolt, they act as independent data controllers from the privacy law perspective. It means that the driver or their fleet is responsible for making the CCTV compliant with the EU requirements. The car should have the warning sign outside or inside the car (visible to the riders) about the CCTV in operation, specification about the purpose of CCTV, who the controller of this data is (name of the fleet or driver (if it’s a private driver), when this data will be deleted, and information where to read the detailed information about the CCTV. 

*From our side, we can contact the fleet (or the driver if they’re a private driver) about this situation and:*

* *Request the Privacy Policy outlining how personal data from the CCTV are being processed to provide it to the rider*
* Advice them to make the CCTV surveillance compliant with the Estonian and EU laws (add to the CCTV warning sign specification about the purpose of CCTV, who the controller of this data is (name of the fleet or driver (if it’s a private driver), when this data will be deleted, and information where to read the detailed information about the CCTV).
* Until they make such changes they may be in breach of privacy laws in terms of their obligation to inform data subjects about the processing (Art. 12 of the GDPR)
* *Advise them* to remove the CCTV until the above is fixed
* *Let them know* that if the rider is considering launching a formal complaint about this situation to the Data Protection Authority

Please note that the fleet or the driver (if they’re a private driver) *are not obliged to follow our advice since they are independent controller and accountable under the GDPR for any violations.*

x.card_label AS KEY, -- card_bin-card_last4:card_expiration_yyyy_mm:card_country
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) AS count_users, -- count of users that use the same card_label
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_orders, -- count of finished orders with the same card_label
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.wallet_card_label IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id END) AS count_wallet_orders, -- count of finished orders with a payment method that goes through user_mobile_wallet_payment_check checkpoint
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.wallet_card_label IS NOT NULL THEN x.order_id END)*1.000/COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS double),3),0) AS wallet_count_ratio, -- ratio of orders where the card is behing a wallet
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.user_price_eur) AS double),2) AS sum_eur, -- amount of finished orders that were paid for by a card_label 
COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.is_final_failed_payment THEN x.order_id END),0) AS count_fp, -- count of orders that are failed payments
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.is_final_failed_payment THEN x.order_id END),0)*1.000/COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) AS double),3),0) AS fp_ratio, -- failed payment ratio based on the count of orders
ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_final_failed_payment THEN x.uncovered_eur ELSE 0 END) AS double),2) AS fp_sum, -- amount of debt from the failed payment orders
ROUND(CAST(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_final_failed_payment THEN x.uncovered_eur ELSE 0 END) AS double),2)*1.000/ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.user_price_eur) AS double),2) AS double),3) AS fp_sum_ratio, -- failed payment ratio based on the amounts
COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem OR x.is_chargeback THEN x.order_id END),0) AS count_fraud, -- count of orders that are chargebacks or payment problems
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem OR x.is_chargeback THEN x.order_id END)*1.000/COUNT (DISTINCT x.order_id) AS double),3),0) AS fraud_ratio, -- fraud (cb, pp) ratio based on the count of orders
ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem OR x.is_chargeback THEN x.user_price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS double),2) AS sum_fraud, -- sum of fraud (cb, pp) payments
ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem OR x.is_chargeback THEN x.user_price_eur ELSE 0 END)*1.000/SUM(x.user_price_eur) AS double),3) AS fraud_sum_ratio -- fraud (cb, pp) ratio based on the amounts
FROM (
WITH wallet_cards AS (
SELECT 
a.meta.order_id AS search_token,
a.meta.city_id AS city_id,
get_json_object(a.input, '$.data.card_metadata.iin') || '-' || get_json_object(a.input, '$.data.card_metadata.last4') || ':' || substr(get_json_object(a.input, '$.data.card_metadata.expiration_date'),1,7) || ':' || lower(get_json_object(a.input, '$.data.card_metadata.country_code')) AS card_label
FROM archive_analytical.user_mobile_wallet_payment_check a
WHERE a.created_hour >= DATEADD(MONTH, -3, CURRENT_DATE)
)
SELECT DISTINCT 
co.order_id,
co.user_id,
co.is_final_failed_payment,
co.is_payment_problem,
co.is_chargeback,
co.user_price_eur,
COALESCE(co.uncovered_amount/co.eur_currency_rate,0) AS uncovered_eur,
wc.card_label AS wallet_card_label,
COALESCE((get_json_object(fc.input, '$.card_info.card_bin') || '-' || get_json_object(fc.input, '$.card_info.card_last4') || ':' || get_json_object(fc.input, '$.card_info.expires') || ':' || lower(get_json_object(fc.input, '$.card_info.card_country')) || ':' || co.order_type),(wc.card_label || ':' || co.order_type),(get_json_object(fc2.input, '$.additional.card.card_bin') || '-' || get_json_object(fc2.input, '$.additional.card.card_last4') || ':' || get_json_object(fc2.input, '$.additional.card.expires') || ':' || lower(get_json_object(fc2.input, '$.additional.card.card_country')) || ':' || co.order_type)) AS card_label
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co
LEFT JOIN archive_analytical.user_order_request fc ON fc.id = co.fraud_calculation_id AND fc.created_hour >= DATEADD(MONTH, -3, CURRENT_DATE)
LEFT JOIN archive_analytical.user_rental_request fc2 ON fc2.id = co.fraud_calculation_id AND fc2.created_hour >= DATEADD(MONTH, -3, CURRENT_DATE)
LEFT JOIN wallet_cards wc ON wc.city_id = co.city_id AND wc.search_token = COALESCE(co.search_token,co.order_id)
WHERE co.created_date >= DATEADD(MONTH, -3, CURRENT_DATE)
AND co.order_state = 'finished' 	
AND co.payment_method_group IN ('in-app','bolt_credit')											
AND co.payment_method_type <> 'business'
AND co.order_type IN ('rides','rental')
) AS x 
WHERE x.card_label IS NOT NULL 
GROUP BY 1
HAVING ((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.uncovered_eur > 0 THEN x.order_id END) > 2 
AND ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_final_failed_payment THEN x.uncovered_eur ELSE 0 END) AS double),2) > 100)
OR (COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem OR x.is_chargeback THEN x.order_id END)*1.000/COUNT (DISTINCT x.order_id) AS double),3),0) >= 0.2 AND ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem OR x.is_chargeback THEN x.user_price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS double),2) > 100)
OR (ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem OR x.is_chargeback THEN x.user_price_eur ELSE 0 END)*1.000/SUM(x.user_price_eur) AS double),3) >= 0.2 AND ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem OR x.is_chargeback THEN x.user_price_eur ELSE 0 END) AS double),2) > 100)){code}

Hey Fabijan,

technically, yes, however, I should highlight some aspects:

1. Entering into the Data Sharing Agreement does not automatically mean that we have a legal basis. We should have a legal basis to share this data, firstly, with APIS IT, and then sign the DSA outlining this sharing.
2. APIS IT, most likely, is a data processor of the Ministry for the processing activity related to this data. It means that the Ministry defines which sets of data can be gathered, the purposes and means and instructs APIS IT to process this data on behalf of the Ministry. It means that APIS IT can reject signing this DSA.
3. In case we will not be able to rely on a legal obligation for testing the software, it’s better for us to try relying on our legitimate interest for sharing the data with the Ministry rather than APIS IT. 
4. In any case, we will, most likely, be able to share this data with the Ministry when testing the software, we just need to see the request for testing the software so that we can rely on the correct legal basis, but there are no any blockers from our side 🙂

Hi Tatsiana! 



Sorry, I somehow missed your previous response. Thank you for the explanations! 



So for scooters, we have more or less two kinds of insurance: 

# Personal accident, i.e damage to riders. All our insurance providers said that they have not imposed any expiration date for submitting claims. In general, they expect a claim to be submitted as soon as possible after the damage exposed itself (for example it might take a while before a person realises they have sustained brain damage), and they’re willing to process these claims without any time limit. For reference - the amount of time how long insurers keep personal data varies - but mostly it’s up to 10 years. 
# RGL/MTPL - these 2 are third-party liability, in practice the insurers are willing to pay out claims according to local laws. Meaning that as long as a claim has not expired according to the local law, the insurers are willing to process the claim. For example, in Estonia, it can be 3 years or 10 years, depending on the type of damage/claim. To get an overview of every specific country, we would probably need input from our field legal councils. 



I don’t know if we can justify ourselves for keeping personal data for 10 years as well but I think it’s obvious that I’m advocating to keep the data as long as possible 🙃  For one, because having it fragmented according to local laws, will make our processes very complicated, and prone to human errors. 

But also because we have unpleasant examples where personal data was deleted - recently a lawyer submitted a claim on behalf of a French woman who sustained injuries in Malta in 2019, and we are struggling to track down what exactly happened because the user account was deleted and we did not have all the details left in our system. So now we’re unable to see if this could be covered with insurance, or whether Bolt should take on the claim.



Hope this is helpful, and happy to get any other details from the insurers if necessary.



Best

Karmel

# _The other calculating_ *_driver's offline hours_*

_When the driver takes a break (goes offline, or is blocked due to exceeding max online hours limit), the offline hour timer starts counting. Hi Jannis,

I have reviewed the process and it is generally aligned with privacy standard expressed in our global Policy on using CCTV, however I’d like to flag one requirement that maybe is not fully expressed in the SOP.

It is obligatory to install warning signs on the premises where video surveillance is carried out (such as via sticker as mentioned in the document). The information should be positioned in such a way that the data subject can easily recognise the circumstances of the surveillance before entering the monitored area (approximately at eye level). 

The warning sign should provide the following information:

* Information that there is video surveillance in the area (e.g camera picture, “We have video surveillance”)
* Information of the controller
* *Information of where further information can be found (QR code or link to the* [*global privacy notice on video surveillance*|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-video-surveillance]*)  - it is mandatory to provide this additional resource to fully deliver on the notification requirements.*

Otherwise, no other concerns from privacy side, also, as Merve has already mentioned, the written consent from employees/3PL is not required.

How it works from our side.

Every Monday we make a _payout_ to the Partner and sent an _invoice_ by e-mail with sums of agency fee and other fees, that Partner must pay to us. Then on Thursdays, UHY sends _Agent reports_ via Vchasno. It is possible that there can be disputes from Partner’s side according to the sums in the invoice, but it is better to fix them before issuing the Agent report. Till the end of the week, Partner must _pay_ our commission for the previous period.

In the draft, I see reverse order in the issuing documents Payout>>*Agent report>>Invoice*>>Payment. So I am not sure that is relevant to our usual approach with other Partners.
